questions.q: Chart shows city pollution rising 2015–2024. Which sentence belongs: 'Pollution rose steadily from 45 to 78 AQI' or 'This is because people buy too many cars'?
questions.a: The first — reports the figure; the second speculates a cause, which is banned. A wrong answer reveals the student thinks analysis means explaining WHY — in this genre it means reporting WHAT, precisely.

questions.q: Rewrite for the genre: 'I think the graph shows very bad pollution.'
questions.a: 'The graph indicates a rise in pollution from X to Y' — report verb + cited data. A wrong answer keeping 'I think' or 'very bad' shows the student hasn't adopted the impersonal-observer stance the paragraph requires.

questions.q: What goes in sentence 1 of an analytical paragraph?
questions.a: The frame — what the data shows and its scope ('The bar chart depicts literacy rates in four states between 2011 and 2021'). A wrong answer jumping straight to a figure shows the student doesn't know the reader needs the map before the territory.

questions.q: Required: report verbs (shows/indicates/reveals), ______, and data citation.
Fill in the blank: The ______ paragraph describes a chart/table in ~100–120 words: identify what the data shows, report the trend and the extremes, compare — never opine.
Fill in the blank: (3) 'X peaked at 62% in 2019, compared to Y at 31%' (extremes + ______).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Given a chart, the student writes a 3-part analytical paragraph (what the data is → main trend → key comparison) with zero opinion, correct report verbs, and at least two cited figures.
